audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Samuel 9, first-pass restored draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for servant agency, women at well, gift/custom issues, seer terminology, private revelation, Saul's body description, Benjamin status, royal-leader vocabulary, and anti-leader-cult safeguards.

verses.restored: There was a man of Benjamin whose name was Kish son of Abiel, son of Zeror, son of Becorath, son of Aphiah, a Benjaminite, a man of standing.

familiar.text: Now there was a man of Benjamin, whose name was Kish, the son of Abiel, the son of Zeror, the son of Bechorath, the son of Aphiah, a Benjamite, a mighty man of power.

modern.text: Now there was a Benjamite, a powerful man, whose name was Kish son of Abiel, the son of Zeror, the son of Becorath, the son of Aphiah of Benjamin.

original.text: וַֽיְהִי אִ֣ישׁ מבן ימין וּ֠שְׁמוֹ קִ֣ישׁ בֶּן אֲבִיאֵ֞ל בֶּן צְר֧וֹר בֶּן בְּכוֹרַ֛ת בֶּן אֲפִ֖יחַ בֶּן אִ֣ישׁ יְמִינִ֑י גִּבּ֖וֹר חָֽיִל

verses.restored: He had a son whose name was Saul, a choice and handsome young man; no Israelite was more handsome than he, and from his shoulders upward he was taller than all the people.

familiar.text: And he had a son, whose name was Saul, a choice young man, and a goodly: and there was not among the children of Israel a goodlier person than he: from his shoulders and upward he was higher than any of the people.

modern.text: And he had a son named Saul, choice and handsome, without equal among the Israelites—a head taller than any of the people.

original.text: וְלוֹ הָיָ֨ה בֵ֜ן וּשְׁמ֤וֹ שָׁאוּל֙ בָּח֣וּר וָט֔וֹב וְאֵ֥ין אִ֛ישׁ מִבְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל ט֣וֹב מִמֶּ֑נּוּ מִשִּׁכְמ֣וֹ וָמַ֔עְלָה גָּבֹ֖הַּ מִכָּל הָעָֽם

verses.restored: The female donkeys of Kish, Saul's father, were lost. Kish said to Saul his son, Take, please, one of the servants with you, arise, and go seek the donkeys.

familiar.text: And the asses of Kish Saul’s father were lost. And Kish said to Saul his son, Take now one of the servants with thee, and arise, go seek the asses.

modern.text: One day the donkeys of Saul’s father Kish wandered off, and Kish said to his son Saul, “Take one of the servants and go look for the donkeys.”

original.text: וַתֹּאבַ֨דְנָה֙ הָאֲתֹנ֔וֹת לְקִ֖ישׁ אֲבִ֣י שָׁא֑וּל וַיֹּ֨אמֶר קִ֜ישׁ אֶל שָׁא֣וּל בְּנ֗וֹ קַח נָ֤א אִתְּךָ֙ אֶת אַחַ֣ד מֵֽהַנְּעָרִ֔ים וְק֣וּם לֵ֔ךְ בַּקֵּ֖שׁ אֶת הָאֲתֹנֹֽת

verses.restored: He passed through hill country of Ephraim and through land of Shalishah, but they did not find them. They passed through land of Shaalim, and they were not there; he passed through land of Benjamin, but they did not find them.

familiar.text: And he passed through mount Ephraim, and passed through the land of Shalisha, but they found them not: then they passed through the land of Shalim, and there they were not: and he passed through the land of the Benjamites, but they found them not.

modern.text: So Saul passed through the hill country of Ephraim and then through the land of Shalishah, but did not find the donkeys. He and the servant went through the region of Shaalim, but they were not there. Then they went through the land of Benjamin, and still they did not find them.

original.text: וַיַּעֲבֹ֧ר בְּהַר אֶפְרַ֛יִם וַיַּעֲבֹ֥ר בְּאֶֽרֶץ שָׁלִ֖שָׁה וְלֹ֣א מָצָ֑אוּ וַיַּעַבְר֤וּ בְאֶֽרֶץ שַׁעֲלִים֙ וָאַ֔יִן וַיַּעֲבֹ֥ר בְּאֶֽרֶץ יְמִינִ֖י וְלֹ֥א מָצָֽאוּ

verses.restored: They came to land of Zuph, and Saul said to his servant who was with him, Come, let us return, lest my father stop caring about donkeys and become anxious about us.

familiar.text: And when they were come to the land of Zuph, Saul said to his servant that was with him, Come, and let us return; lest my father leave caring for the asses, and take thought for us.

modern.text: When they reached the land of Zuph, Saul said to his servant, “Come, let us go back, or my father will stop worrying about the donkeys and start worrying about us.”

original.text: הֵ֗מָּה בָּ֚אוּ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ צ֔וּף וְשָׁא֥וּל אָמַ֛ר לְנַעֲר֥וֹ אֲשֶׁר עִמּ֖וֹ לְכָ֣ה וְנָשׁ֑וּבָה פֶּן יֶחְדַּ֥ל אָבִ֛י מִן הָאֲתֹנ֖וֹת וְדָ֥אַג לָֽנוּ

verses.restored: He said to him, Look, please, a man of Divine is in this city, and the man is honored; all that he says surely comes to pass. Now let us go there; perhaps he will tell us our way upon which we have gone.

familiar.text: And he said unto him, Behold now, there is in this city a man of God, and he is an honourable man; all that he saith cometh surely to pass: now let us go thither; peradventure he can shew us our way that we should go.

modern.text: “Look,” said the servant, “in this city there is a man of God who is highly respected; everything he says surely comes to pass. Let us go there now. Perhaps he will tell us which way to go.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ הִנֵּה נָ֤א אִישׁ אֱלֹהִים֙ בָּעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֔את וְהָאִ֣ישׁ נִכְבָּ֔ד כֹּ֥ל אֲשֶׁר יְדַבֵּ֖ר בּ֣וֹא יָב֑וֹא עַתָּה֙ נֵ֣לֲכָה שָּׁ֔ם אוּלַי֙ יַגִּ֣יד לָ֔נוּ אֶת דַּרְכֵּ֖נוּ אֲשֶׁר הָלַ֥כְנוּ עָלֶֽיהָ

verses.restored: Saul said to his servant, But look, if we go, what shall we bring the man? Bread is gone from our vessels, and there is no gift to bring to man of Divine. What is with us?

familiar.text: Then said Saul to his servant, But, behold, if we go, what shall we bring the man? for the bread is spent in our vessels, and there is not a present to bring to the man of God: what have we?

modern.text: “If we do go,” Saul replied, “what can we give the man? For the bread in our packs is gone, and there is no gift to take to the man of God. What do we have?”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שָׁא֜וּל לְנַעֲר֗וֹ וְהִנֵּ֣ה נֵלֵךְ֮ וּמַה נָּבִ֣יא לָאִישׁ֒ כִּ֤י הַלֶּ֨חֶם֙ אָזַ֣ל מִכֵּלֵ֔ינוּ וּתְשׁוּרָ֥ה אֵין לְהָבִ֖יא לְאִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים מָ֖ה אִתָּֽנוּ

verses.restored: The servant answered Saul again and said, Look, there is found in my hand a quarter shekel of silver. I will give it to man of Divine, and he will tell us our way.

familiar.text: And the servant answered Saul again, and said, Behold, I have here at hand the fourth part of a shekel of silver: that will I give to the man of God, to tell us our way.

modern.text: The servant answered him again. “Look,” he said, “I have here in my hand a quarter shekel of silver. I will give it to the man of God, and he will tell us our way.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤סֶף הַנַּ֨עַר֙ לַעֲנ֣וֹת אֶת שָׁא֔וּל וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הִנֵּה֙ נִמְצָ֣א בְיָדִ֔י רֶ֖בַע שֶׁ֣קֶל כָּ֑סֶף וְנָֽתַתִּי֙ לְאִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וְהִגִּ֥יד לָ֖נוּ אֶת דַּרְכֵּֽנוּ

verses.restored: Formerly in Israel, thus a person said when going to inquire of Divine: Come, let us go to seer; for prophet of today was formerly called seer.

familiar.text: (Beforetime in Israel, when a man went to enquire of God, thus he spake, Come, and let us go to the seer: for he that is now called a Prophet was beforetime called a Seer.)

modern.text: (Formerly in Israel, a man on his way to inquire of God would say, “Come, let us go to the seer.” For the prophet of today was formerly called the seer.)

original.text: לְפָנִ֣ים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר הָאִישׁ֙ בְּלֶכְתּוֹ֙ לִדְר֣וֹשׁ אֱלֹהִ֔ים לְכ֥וּ וְנֵלְכָ֖ה עַד הָרֹאֶ֑ה כִּ֤י לַנָּבִיא֙ הַיּ֔וֹם יִקָּרֵ֥א לְפָנִ֖ים הָרֹאֶֽה

verses.restored: Saul said to his servant, Your word is good; come, let us go. And they went to city where man of Divine was.

familiar.text: Then said Saul to his servant, Well said; come, let us go. So they went unto the city where the man of God was.

modern.text: “Good,” said Saul to his servant. “Come, let us go.” So they set out for the city where the man of God was.

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שָׁא֧וּל לְנַעֲר֛וֹ ט֥וֹב דְּבָרְךָ֖ לְכָ֣ה נֵלֵ֑כָה וַיֵּֽלְכוּ֙ אֶל הָעִ֔יר אֲשֶׁר שָׁ֖ם אִ֥ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִֽים

verses.restored: As they were going up ascent to city, they found young women going out to draw water and said to them, Is seer here?

familiar.text: And as they went up the hill to the city, they found young maidens going out to draw water, and said unto them, Is the seer here?

modern.text: And as they were climbing the hill to the city, they met some young women coming out to draw water and asked, “Is the seer here?”

original.text: הֵ֗מָּה עֹלִים֙ בְּמַעֲלֵ֣ה הָעִ֔יר וְהֵ֨מָּה֙ מָצְא֣וּ נְעָר֔וֹת יֹצְא֖וֹת לִשְׁאֹ֣ב מָ֑יִם וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ לָהֶ֔ן הֲיֵ֥שׁ בָּזֶ֖ה הָרֹאֶֽה

verses.restored: They answered them and said, He is; look, he is before you. Hurry now, for today he came to city because people have a sacrifice today at high place.

familiar.text: And they answered them, and said, He is; behold, he is before you: make haste now, for he came to day to the city; for there is a sacrifice of the people to day in the high place:

modern.text: “Yes, he is ahead of you,” they answered. “Hurry now, for today he has come to the city because the people have a sacrifice on the high place.

original.text: וַתַּעֲנֶ֧ינָה אוֹתָ֛ם וַתֹּאמַ֥רְנָה יֵּ֖שׁ הִנֵּ֣ה לְפָנֶ֑יךָ מַהֵ֣ר עַתָּ֗ה כִּ֤י הַיּוֹם֙ בָּ֣א לָעִ֔יר כִּ֣י זֶ֧בַח הַיּ֛וֹם לָעָ֖ם בַּבָּמָֽה

verses.restored: As you enter city, you will find him before he goes up to high place to eat. People will not eat until he comes, for he blesses sacrifice; afterward those invited eat. Now go up, for about this time you will find him.

familiar.text: As soon as ye be come into the city, ye shall straightway find him, before he go up to the high place to eat: for the people will not eat until he come, because he doth bless the sacrifice; and afterwards they eat that be bidden. Now therefore get you up; for about this time ye shall find him.

modern.text: As soon as you enter the city, you will find him before he goes up to the high place to eat. The people will not eat until he comes, because he must bless the sacrifice; after that, the guests will eat. Go up at once; you will find him.”

original.text: כְּבֹאֲכֶ֣ם הָעִ֣יר כֵּ֣ן תִּמְצְא֣וּן אֹת֡וֹ בְּטֶרֶם֩ יַעֲלֶ֨ה הַבָּמָ֜תָה לֶאֱכֹ֗ל כִּ֠י לֹֽא יֹאכַ֤ל הָעָם֙ עַד בֹּא֔וֹ כִּֽי הוּא֙ יְבָרֵ֣ךְ הַזֶּ֔בַח אַחֲרֵי כֵ֖ן יֹאכְל֣וּ הַקְּרֻאִ֑ים וְעַתָּ֣ה עֲל֔וּ כִּֽי אֹת֥וֹ כְהַיּ֖וֹם תִּמְצְא֥וּן אֹתֽוֹ

verses.restored: They went up to city. As they entered within city, look, Samuel was coming out toward them to go up to high place.

familiar.text: And they went up into the city: and when they were come into the city, behold, Samuel came out against them, for to go up to the high place.

modern.text: So Saul and his servant went up toward the city, and as they were entering it, there was Samuel coming toward them on his way up to the high place.

original.text: וַֽיַּעֲל֖וּ הָעִ֑יר הֵ֗מָּה בָּאִים֙ בְּת֣וֹךְ הָעִ֔יר וְהִנֵּ֤ה שְׁמוּאֵל֙ יֹצֵ֣א לִקְרָאתָ֔ם לַעֲל֖וֹת הַבָּמָֽה

verses.restored: Now YHWH had uncovered Samuel's ear one day before Saul came, saying,

familiar.text: Now the LORD had told Samuel in his ear a day before Saul came, saying,

modern.text: Now on the day before Saul’s arrival, the LORD had revealed to Samuel,

original.text: וַֽיהוָ֔ה גָּלָ֖ה אֶת אֹ֣זֶן שְׁמוּאֵ֑ל י֣וֹם אֶחָ֔ד לִפְנֵ֥י בֽוֹא שָׁא֖וּל לֵאמֹֽר

verses.restored: About this time tomorrow I will send to you a man from land of Benjamin. You shall anoint him as leader over my people Israel, and he shall save my people from hand of Philistines, for I have seen my people because their cry has come to me.

familiar.text: To morrow about this time I will send thee a man out of the land of Benjamin, and thou shalt anoint him to be captain over my people Israel, that he may save my people out of the hand of the Philistines: for I have looked upon my people, because their cry is come unto me.

modern.text: “At this time tomorrow I will send you a man from the land of Benjamin, and you are to anoint him leader over My people Israel; he will save them from the hand of the Philistines. For I have looked upon My people, because their cry has come to Me.”

original.text: כָּעֵ֣ת מָחָ֡ר אֶשְׁלַח֩ אֵלֶ֨יךָ אִ֜ישׁ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ בִּנְיָמִ֗ן וּמְשַׁחְתּ֤וֹ לְנָגִיד֙ עַל עַמִּ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְהוֹשִׁ֥יעַ אֶת עַמִּ֖י מִיַּ֣ד פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים כִּ֤י רָאִ֨יתִי֙ אֶת עַמִּ֔י כִּ֛י בָּ֥אָה צַעֲקָת֖וֹ אֵלָֽי

verses.restored: When Samuel saw Saul, YHWH answered him, Look, the man of whom I spoke to you; this one shall restrain/govern my people.

familiar.text: And when Samuel saw Saul, the LORD said unto him, Behold the man whom I spake to thee of! this same shall reign over my people.

modern.text: When Samuel saw Saul, the LORD told him, “Here is the man of whom I spoke; he shall rule over My people.”

original.text: וּשְׁמוּאֵ֖ל רָאָ֣ה אֶת שָׁא֑וּל וַיהוָ֣ה עָנָ֔הוּ הִנֵּ֤ה הָאִישׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָמַ֣רְתִּי אֵלֶ֔יךָ זֶ֖ה יַעְצֹ֥ר בְּעַמִּֽי

verses.restored: Saul approached Samuel in middle of gate and said, Tell me, please, where house of seer is.

familiar.text: Then Saul drew near to Samuel in the gate, and said, Tell me, I pray thee, where the seer’s house is.

modern.text: Saul approached Samuel in the gateway and asked, “Would you please tell me where the seer’s house is?”

original.text: וַיִּגַּ֥שׁ שָׁא֛וּל אֶת שְׁמוּאֵ֖ל בְּת֣וֹךְ הַשָּׁ֑עַר וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הַגִּֽידָה נָּ֣א לִ֔י אֵי זֶ֖ה בֵּ֥ית הָרֹאֶֽה

verses.restored: Samuel answered Saul and said, I am seer. Go up before me to high place, and you shall eat with me today. In morning I will send you away, and all that is in your heart I will tell you.

familiar.text: And Samuel answered Saul, and said, I am the seer: go up before me unto the high place; for ye shall eat with me to day, and to morrow I will let thee go, and will tell thee all that is in thine heart.

modern.text: “I am the seer,” Samuel replied. “Go up before me to the high place, for you shall eat with me today. And when I send you off in the morning, I will tell you all that is in your heart.

original.text: וַיַּ֨עַן שְׁמוּאֵ֜ל אֶת שָׁא֗וּל וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אָנֹכִ֣י הָרֹאֶ֔ה עֲלֵ֤ה לְפָנַי֙ הַבָּמָ֔ה וַאֲכַלְתֶּ֥ם עִמִּ֖י הַיּ֑וֹם וְשִׁלַּחְתִּ֣יךָ בַבֹּ֔קֶר וְכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר בִּֽלְבָבְךָ֖ אַגִּ֥יד לָֽךְ

verses.restored: As for donkeys lost to you three days ago, do not set your heart on them, for they have been found. And toward whom is all desire of Israel? Is it not toward you and toward all house of your father?

familiar.text: And as for thine asses that were lost three days ago, set not thy mind on them; for they are found. And on whom is all the desire of Israel? Is it not on thee, and on all thy father’s house?

modern.text: As for the donkeys you lost three days ago, do not worry about them, for they have been found. And upon whom is all the desire of Israel, if not upon you and all your father’s house?”

original.text: וְלָאֲתֹנ֞וֹת הָאֹבְד֣וֹת לְךָ֗ הַיּוֹם֙ שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת הַיָּמִ֔ים אַל תָּ֧שֶׂם אֶֽת לִבְּךָ֛ לָהֶ֖ם כִּ֣י נִמְצָ֑אוּ וּלְמִי֙ כָּל חֶמְדַּ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הֲל֣וֹא לְךָ֔ וּלְכֹ֖ל בֵּ֥ית אָבִֽיךָ

verses.restored: Saul answered and said, Am I not a Benjaminite, from smallest of tribes of Israel, and my clan smallest of all clans of tribe of Benjamin? Why then have you spoken to me a word like this?

familiar.text: And Saul answered and said, Am not I a Benjamite, of the smallest of the tribes of Israel? and my family the least of all the families of the tribe of Benjamin? wherefore then speakest thou so to me?

modern.text: Saul replied, “Am I not a Benjamite from the smallest tribe of Israel, and is not my clan the least of all the clans of Benjamin? So why would you say such a thing to me?”

original.text: וַיַּ֨עַן שָׁא֜וּל וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הֲל֨וֹא בֶן יְמִינִ֤י אָ֨נֹכִי֙ מִקַּטַנֵּי֙ שִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וּמִשְׁפַּחְתִּי֙ הַצְּעִרָ֔ה מִכָּֽל מִשְׁפְּח֖וֹת שִׁבְטֵ֣י בִנְיָמִ֑ן וְלָ֨מָּה֙ דִּבַּ֣רְתָּ אֵלַ֔י כַּדָּבָ֖ר הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: Samuel took Saul and his servant, brought them into hall, and gave them a place at head of invited guests, about thirty persons.

familiar.text: And Samuel took Saul and his servant, and brought them into the parlour, and made them sit in the chiefest place among them that were bidden, which were about thirty persons.

modern.text: Then Samuel took Saul and his servant, brought them into the hall, and seated them in the place of honor among those who were invited—about thirty in all.

original.text: וַיִּקַּ֤ח שְׁמוּאֵל֙ אֶת שָׁא֣וּל וְאֶֽת נַעֲר֔וֹ וַיְבִיאֵ֖ם לִשְׁכָּ֑תָה וַיִּתֵּ֨ן לָהֶ֤ם מָקוֹם֙ בְּרֹ֣אשׁ הַקְּרוּאִ֔ים וְהֵ֖מָּה כִּשְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים אִֽישׁ

verses.restored: Samuel said to cook, Give portion I gave you, of which I said to you, Set it beside you.

familiar.text: And Samuel said unto the cook, Bring the portion which I gave thee, of which I said unto thee, Set it by thee.

modern.text: And Samuel said to the cook, “Bring the portion I gave you and told you to set aside.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל֙ לַטַּבָּ֔ח תְּנָה֙ אֶת הַמָּנָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֖תִּי לָ֑ךְ אֲשֶׁר֙ אָמַ֣רְתִּי אֵלֶ֔יךָ שִׂ֥ים אֹתָ֖הּ עִמָּֽךְ

verses.restored: The cook lifted thigh and what was upon it and set it before Saul. Samuel said, Look, what was kept is set before you. Eat, because it was kept for you for appointed time, since I said, I have invited people. Saul ate with Samuel that day.

familiar.text: And the cook took up the shoulder, and that which was upon it, and set it before Saul. And Samuel said, Behold that which is left! set it before thee, and eat: for unto this time hath it been kept for thee since I said, I have invited the people. So Saul did eat with Samuel that day.

modern.text: So the cook picked up the leg and what was attached to it and set it before Saul. Then Samuel said, “Here is what was kept back. It was set apart for you. Eat, for it has been kept for you for this occasion, from the time I said, ‘I have invited the people.’” So Saul dined with Samuel that day.

original.text: וַיָּ֣רֶם הַ֠טַּבָּח אֶת הַשּׁ֨וֹק וְהֶעָלֶ֜יהָ וַיָּ֣שֶׂם לִפְנֵ֣י שָׁא֗וּל וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הִנֵּ֤ה הַנִּשְׁאָר֙ שִׂים לְפָנֶ֣יךָ אֱכֹ֔ל כִּ֧י לַמּוֹעֵ֛ד שָֽׁמוּר לְךָ֥ לֵאמֹ֖ר הָעָ֣ם קָרָ֑אתִי וַיֹּ֧אכַל שָׁא֛וּל עִם שְׁמוּאֵ֖ל בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא

verses.restored: They came down from high place to city, and he spoke with Saul upon roof.

familiar.text: And when they were come down from the high place into the city, Samuel communed with Saul upon the top of the house.

modern.text: And after they had come down from the high place into the city, Samuel spoke with Saul on the roof of his house.

original.text: וַיֵּרְד֥וּ מֵהַבָּמָ֖ה הָעִ֑יר וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר עִם שָׁא֖וּל עַל הַגָּֽג

verses.restored: They arose early. At break of dawn Samuel called to Saul upon roof, saying, Rise, and I will send you away. Saul arose, and the two of them, he and Samuel, went outside.

familiar.text: And they arose early: and it came to pass about the spring of the day, that Samuel called Saul to the top of the house, saying, Up, that I may send thee away. And Saul arose, and they went out both of them, he and Samuel, abroad.

modern.text: They got up early in the morning, and just before dawn Samuel called to Saul on the roof, “Get ready, and I will send you on your way!” So Saul arose, and both he and Samuel went outside together.

original.text: וַיַּשְׁכִּ֗מוּ וַיְהִ֞י כַּעֲל֤וֹת הַשַּׁ֨חַר֙ וַיִּקְרָ֨א שְׁמוּאֵ֤ל אֶל שָׁאוּל֙ הגג לֵאמֹ֔ר ק֖וּמָה וַאֲשַׁלְּחֶ֑ךָּ וַיָּ֣קָם שָׁא֗וּל וַיֵּצְא֧וּ שְׁנֵיהֶ֛ם ה֥וּא וּשְׁמוּאֵ֖ל הַחֽוּצָה

verses.restored: As they were going down at edge of city, Samuel said to Saul, Say to servant that he pass before us—and he passed on—but you stand now, and I will cause you to hear word of Divine.

familiar.text: And as they were going down to the end of the city, Samuel said to Saul, Bid the servant pass on before us, (and he passed on), but stand thou still a while, that I may shew thee the word of God.

modern.text: As they were going down to the edge of the city, Samuel said to Saul, “Tell the servant to go on ahead of us, but you stay for a while, and I will reveal to you the word of God.” So the servant went on.

original.text: הֵ֗מָּה יֽוֹרְדִים֙ בִּקְצֵ֣ה הָעִ֔יר וּשְׁמוּאֵ֞ל אָמַ֣ר אֶל שָׁא֗וּל אֱמֹ֥ר לַנַּ֛עַר וְיַעֲבֹ֥ר לְפָנֵ֖ינוּ וַֽיַּעֲבֹ֑ר וְאַתָּה֙ עֲמֹ֣ד כַּיּ֔וֹם וְאַשְׁמִיעֲךָ֖ אֶת דְּבַ֥ר אֱלֹהִֽים

translation_notes: Saul begins not as a conqueror but as a son searching for lost animals with a servant whose practical knowledge redirects the journey.
The servant is an active guide and financial contributor; class status does not make his insight secondary.
The young women at the well provide essential public information and are not romanticized or treated as scenery.
'Seer' and 'prophet' reflect historical terminology; spiritual authority must not be bought, although customary gifts supported consultation.
Saul's height and appearance are narrative features, not proof of fitness, masculinity, Divine favor, or leadership worth.
The verb in verse 17 can carry restrain, govern, or hold back; kingship enters with ambiguity rather than uncomplicated celebration.
Anointing is presented as response to the people's cry under Philistine pressure. It does not place Saul beyond accountability.
Benjamin's smallness and Saul's self-description must not support ethnic hierarchy, false humility tests, or leader cults.
safety_note: Do not turn physical attractiveness, height, ancestry, private revelation, ceremonial seating, or anointing into proof that a leader deserves obedience. Do not erase servants or women whose knowledge enables the story. Prophetic consultation may not be commercialized into spiritual exploitation.
